chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who marries the woman for a specified term: if he brings her dower by the specified term, she is his wife; but if he does not bring her dower by the term, there is no authority for him over her. And that is their stipulation between them when they married her, so he judged for the man that in his hand is the body (possession) of his wife, and he nullified their stipulation.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fixed-term marriage if the dower is not paid on time?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that in fixed-term marriage, the timely payment of the dower serves as the condition for retaining conjugal rights (buz'), while failure to pay nullifies this right, effectively invalidating the marital bond despite the initial contract. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the dower is not merely a gift but a substantive condition governing the validity of the husband's authority over the wife, distinguishing it from the general Sunni understanding of dower as an obligatory but non--conditioning element of marriage.
